title.narrative: Corridors of Hope II HIV/AIDS Prevention Initiative (COH II)

description.narrative: The Corridors of Hope II HIV/AIDS Prevention Initiative (COH II) aims to decrease HIV transmission, morbidity, and mortality among the general population in seven of the highest-prevalence border and corridor communities in Zambia. The initiative engages local leaders and local governmental and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) to play a central role in the projects design, implementation, and evaluation. Its primary strategy is to change community norms of sexual behavior, especially among groups at greatest risk. COH IIs prevention services include behavior change communication and social mobilization interventions, diagnosis and treatment of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), expanded HIV counseling and testing services, and strengthened referral networks. All activities closely involve the border and corridor communities themselves to help change the key social norms affecting HIV transmission. The project also links women with organizations that help with legal protection and that assist aspiring women entrepreneurs. The program has seen broad successes in behavio change to decrease HIV risk.

Interventions will ensure that teachers are proficient in literacy instruction to teach students essential literacy skills needed to learn other subjects. The activity also establishes public-private partnerships to leverage resources to support the delivery of quality education to improve learning outcomes. title.narrative: Scaling Up Nutrition Technical Assistance (SUN TA)

description.narrative: (Zambia): .The Scaling Up Nutrition Technical Assistance activity works through the Zambian government to reduce stunting among children under age two in 13 national districts. It aims to address the drivers of stunting including: 1) inadequate dietary diversity among women and children; 2) achieving minimally acceptable diets for children under two years of age; 3) promoting health-seeking behaviors including family planning, maternal and child health; and 4) increasing access to safe drinking water and improved sanitation. With FY 2022 funds, USAID will provide technical assistance to strengthen the delivery of high-priority maternal child health interventions that will lower the rates of diarrheal illness and improve appropriate management of diarrhea, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and agriculture interventions to reduce stunting. The activity will support households with pregnant and lactating women through Social Behavior Change interventions, and family planning training and commodities to communities to expand access to family planning services and promotion of contraceptive use. Further, the funds will support counseling on maternal and/or child nutrition. District and village level Water Sanitation and Hygiene champions will be trained to improve sanitation and access to safe water, new wells will be drilled and old ones will be rehabilitated. The activity will promote household food security by supporting contract farming with private sector partners. Under USAID's CDCS, the mechanism will support Development Objective 2: Rural Poverty Reduced through Enterprise-Driven, Inclusive Economic Growth, and Development Objective 3: Capacity of Zambia's Government, Citizens and Private Sector Increased to Improve Health Outcomes and Meet Critical Needs of Vulnerable Populations. This mechanism contributes directly to the Administration's policy priority of building global health security capacity by investing in basic health care systems. .

description.narrative: (Zambia): Zambia's high rates of malnutrition-based child stunting have persisted for several decades at up to 45-50 percent in rural areas. SUN LE is the learning and evaluation arm of the entire MCDP, including USAID's Scaling Up Nutrition Technical Assistance mechanism. This includes identifying, designing, and testing solutions to more effectively understand and measure outcomes to attain the GRZ and donors' joint goal of reducing stunting. Fiscal Year 2022 funds will be used to conduct a performance assessment and focused studies on the implementation of GRZ nutrition services to promote learning around stunting issues, to inform the greater GRZ and multi-donor supported MCDP and support the upgrade of the National Food and Nutrition Commission website to allow the posting of the nutrition research and communications products. SUN LE will be collecting and disseminating data to identify and promote development breakthroughs around stunting and use the data to modify and improve activities. This mechanism prevents stunting in future generations and supports USAID's Development Objective 3: Capacity of Zambia's Government, Citizens and Private Sector Increased to Improve Health Outcomes and Meet Critical Needs of Vulnerable Populations. This mechanism contributes directly to the Administration priority of building global health security capacity by investing in basic health care systems..

description.narrative: (Zambia): The Enterprise Development and Growth Enhanced (EDGE) activity provides technical assistance to financial intermediaries to strengthen their capacity to lend to rural enterprises and improve management capacities of small and medium sized agricultural enterprises (SMEs). FY 2022 funds will support activities working with finance institutions to design financial products and services relevant to the needs of rural enterprises; strengthen their lending capacity; and design ways to simplify the lending process to reduce the costs of lending. It will also address challenges that private sector enterprises face in opening up opportunities to increase their own customer base and ultimately increase their demand for and effective utilization of financial services. Activities include strengthening the ability of banks and finance institutions to serve SMEs and catalyze the growth of non-bank financial institutions and making SMEs and their products more competitive. The activity also works to strengthen SME management and marketing capacity and improve network input/output relationships. Through a business advisor network, the activity works to support agricultural SMEs to reduce costs and increase efficiency by strengthening managerial capacity and improving their ability to seek and qualify for finance. More efficient and competitive SMEs will increase employment in general, and for youth and women. This approach will increase the profitability of agricultural SMEs by facilitating greater revenue through increased sales and expanding access to new markets with premium sales prices. EDGE supports the Global Food Security Strategy objectives of Reducing Rural Poverty through increased agriculture-led economic growth and expanded markets and trade and the USAID/Zambia Country Development Cooperation Strategy Development Objective 2: Rural Poverty Reduced Through Enterprise-Driven Inclusive Economic Growth.

(Zambia): Over the years, works aimed at enhancing the quality of education in Zambia have predominantly focused on facilitating access and delivering school-based interventions with limited focus on the other core elements which are necessary for an effective and self-sustaining system. USAID will partner with the Government of the Republic of Zambia's (GRZ) Ministry of General Education (MOGE) to improve the capacity of universities and colleges of education to complement, strengthen, and sustain existing investments in early-grade reading. .The Transforming Teacher Education activity will make targeted, foundational investments to institutionalize early-grade reading expertise among faculties at the pre-service level, and devise a practical program of study to prepare teachers for teaching reading at the pre-primary and primary school levels. Using FY 2021 funds and in partnership with US based education institutions, it will directly target principals and lecturers to participate in an intensive course of study in language, literacy, early-grade reading, and differentiated instruction. The activity will also establish two Centers of Excellence housed at the University of Zambia and one of the colleges of education to sustain effective instructional practices, coaching, and mentoring in primary literacy instruction.The activity will complement USAID/Zambia's existing investments, primarily the Let's Read and Teaching at the Right Level (Catch Up) activities which focus on improving the instructional skills of in-service teachers already deployed to schools. This will support achievement of USAID/Zambia CDCS Development Objective 4: Quality of Primary Education Strengthened to Improve Learning Outcomes.It also contributes directly to the Administration policy priority of promoting healthy, educated, and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives..

description.narrative: (Zambia): .The Alternatives to Charcoal (A2C) mechanism will address national-level threats that drive deforestation, in particular, the over-reliance on charcoal for household energy and the lack of sustainable alternative-energy options. Charcoal production results in forest degradation and deforestation, including key habitat for wildlife and associated ecotourism. With FY 2022 funding, A2C will engage the private sector to address market barriers and pilot financing instruments to promote the uptake of alternatives to charcoal, while also introducing policy and regulatory reforms to improve the business enabling environment and regulation of the charcoal sector. During FY 2022, A2C will increase awareness and generate behavioral change in supporting alternative fuels and technologies. A2C will roll out its grants program to support development of innovative products, services, or business models within ATF value chains. A2C will work with Community Forest Management Groups and build the capacity of community-based Honorary Forest Officers. A2C will develop protocols and build the capacity of the Forest Department in forest monitoring of charcoal impacts in targeted districts. The mechanism will collaborate extensively with the Zambian government to establish an enabling environment to support the private sector's role in providing low emission energy options and by improving GRZ capacity for enforcement to reduce illegal charcoal production. The A2C objectives are key to meeting the mission's Development Objective 2: Reduce Rural Poverty through Enterprise-Driven Inclusive Economic Growth. A2C contributes to the U.S. foreign policy priority of working with partner countries to help improve their business environment and move beyond assistance to trade relationships and partnerships that promote prosperity, and the U.S priority areas of addressing climate change mitigation..

(Zambia): Local Impact Governance supports the Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) to strengthen participatory governance and the fiscal capabilities of local authorities for improved development planning, implementation, and performance management. With FY 2022 funds, the activity will: 1) help citizens and the private sector improve their collective skills to assess service delivery and constructively engage with government; 2) strengthen the sub-national governance system to become more responsive to citizen needs, generate revenue, and improve service-delivery outcomes; and 3) generate learning and facilitate problem solving that supports an effective, financially viable sub-national governance system. At the national Level, Local Impact will support the review of the Decentralization Policy to align it with the 2016 Constitution and the new Administration's priorities. The activity will also support the Government of Zambia to kick start sector devolution which is a key enabling approach for national decentralization of service delivery for key district services which are scheduled to be devolved within the next two years. Under USAID/Zambia's Country Development Cooperation Strategy, the activity will support Development Objective 1: Citizen and National Self-Reliance Advanced by More Effective Accountable Governance and IR 1.1 Citizen Engagement in National Development Choices Strengthened and contributes and contributes to IR 1.2 Public Resources more Effectively Used.....

FY 2022 funds will support training and mentorship in high-impact RMNCAH&N interventions; TA for service delivery; promotion of community involvement through focused training and behavior change communications; and targeted health-systems strengthening, including data analysis and data use for decision-making. This includes sustaining prevention and timely care-seeking, buffering disruptions to service delivery, and maximizing the collection, analysis and use of data to improve services. Activities will address water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) needs in health facilities to support infection prevention and control, operation and maintenance of WASH facilities and strengthening optimal hygiene behaviors among health workers and the community. Under USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy, the mechanism will support Development Objective 3: Capacity of Zambia's Government, Citizens and Private Sector Increased to Improve Health Outcomes and Meet Critical Needs of Vulnerable Populations and the Administration policy priority of building global health security capacity by investing in basic health care systems. .

The activity further supports private sector and civil society stakeholders by facilitating effective dialogue and advocacy on taxation and to build coalitions that mobilize support for both revenue mobilization and broader fiscal policy reforms. description.narrative: (Zambia): The Eastern Kafue Nature Alliance (EKNA) aims to achieve biodiversity.conservation and cross-cutting outcomes in food security, nutrition, health,.water, and sanitation in the Greater Kafue Landscape (GKL), which includes.Kafue National Park, Zambia's largest protected area. Unsustainable agriculture,.poaching, overfishing, deforestation, and habitat degradation are major threats.to the biodiversity of the GKL. With FY 2022 funds, EKNA, a partnership with.private sector entities Kashikoto Conservancy Limited and Amatheon AGRI Zambia.Limited, will promote inclusive natural resources governance and support.wildlife and forestry law enforcement, agricultural productivity,.entrepreneurship, and increased access to safe water and maternal and child.health (MCH) services. With FY 2022 funds, the EKNA will provide both training.and technical support to strengthen farmers to adopt more productive climate.resilient agricultural technologies to increase productivity, reduce labor and.water needs, and create empowered, climate-resilient farmers. Private-sector.partnerships will also provide agronomic extension and facilitate linkages to.output markets. EKNA will also harness over $11 million of private sector.leveraged resources and strengthen community natural resources governance.institutions to partner with various stakeholders for improving socio-economic,.health, food security, nutrition, forestry, and wildlife conservation.conditions. This will, in turn, strengthen disincentives for illegal.exploitation of natural resources, while increasing incentives for proper.stewardship and community buy-in to the GKL's biodiversity, thereby improving.and stabilizing long-term economic and livelihood opportunities. (Zambia): In Zambia, policy challenges across many sectors inhibit private sector growth and discourage foreign and domestic investment into local businesses. Market-distorting government interventions in agricultural markets, restrictions on international trade in commodities, and poorly functioning marketing systems deter agribusinesses. In the energy sector, there is a need to expand access to electricity for households and businesses, improve electricity reliability, and diversify electricity generation sources. The Government of Zambia (GRZ) seeks to create one million jobs by 2030 and increase the contribution of wildlife and forests to the country's economic growth through tourism. This goal is stymied by poor policy enforcement and illicit demands on natural resources such as poaching, charcoal production, and timber extraction. The Business Enabling Project (BEP) supports development and implementation of policies and regulations that catalyze private sector investment and trade by strengthening Zambian government and civil society organizations to improve and streamline policies and processes. BEP supports GRZ structures such as the new Public-Private Dialogue Forum and its sector working groups to enhance buy-in and sustainability of the private sector. If the GRZ creates a business-enabling environment that is informed with input from key stakeholders, then private sector companies will be supported to grow their businesses, expand trade and attract increased investment in agriculture, energy, as well as nature-based tourism and natural resource management that support biodiversity conservation. This is anticipated to result in broad-based gender-equitable economic growth that transforms rural areas and pulls people out of poverty.Under USAID's CDCS, the mechanism supports Development Objective 2: Reduce Rural Poverty through Enterprise-Driven Inclusive Economic Growth, andthe Administration's policy priority of private sector engagement..

(Zambia): The Expanding Water and Sanitation activity facilitates the provision of reliable and sustainable Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services to improve household economic and health outcomes and thereby contribute to rural poverty reduction. The project will improve delivery, promote financially sustainable models for construction, operation and maintenance of WASH services. Further, the project will support the regulatory and institutional capacity of government, civil society and private service providers in WASH planning and budgeting as well as in managing, regulating, and monitoring service delivery. Furthermore, the project will train enterprises to provide WASH services such as household latrine construction and operation and maintenance of water facilities. With FY 2022 funds, USAID will support sustainable WASH service delivery, facilitate private sector participation, improve operation and maintenance, promote good governance and accountability to contribute to water and sanitation service provision, and address policy barriers to improved access to WASH services, promoting financially sustainable, climate-smart models for construction, operation and maintenance of WASH services. This will ultimately contribute to achieving the goal of sustainably improving access to safe drinking water and sanitation services by addressing both the water supply and demand side constraints while also addressing the business enabling environment for provision of WASH services. Under USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy, the mechanism will support Development Objective 3: Capacity of Zambia's Government, Citizens and Private Sector to Improve Health and Economic Outcomes and Meet Critical Needs of Vulnerable Populations. More broadly, this mechanism contributes to the U.S. foreign policy priority of working with partner countries to accelerate water security and advance resilience, prosperity, and stability.... ..

description.narrative: (Zambia): The Luangwa Livelihood and Conservation (LLC) activity aims to enhance the resilience and health of natural resource-dependent ecological and human communities in the Luangwa Valley of Zambia. The valley is home to Zambia's only black rhino population and its largest elephant population. The Activity will harness over $10 million in private financing and contribute to strengthening disincentives for illegal activities, while increasing incentives to realize tangible improvements for conservation and human wellbeing. With FY 2022 funding, local communities will benefit from Maternal and Child Health interventions focused on capacity building of community health workers to address household and community level factors that delay or prevent women from seeking ante-natal care or delivery at healthcare facilities. The LLC will also increase access to safe drinking water through provision of basic water supply services such as boreholes. The activity will provide training, supplies and equipment such as communication aids, vehicles, uniforms, and rations to Wildlife Police Officers and Community Scouts to undertake effective resource protection operations. In addition, support will improve strategic law enforcement coordination among law enforcement agencies. The activity will support the development of livelihood hubs which will serve as community centers for stimulating economic opportunities for over 100,000 beneficiaries. Farmers will receive support for market access, training and mentoring in improved agricultural techniques, and farming techniques for new crops (chili, honey) to promote improved food security. Together these cross-cutting outcomes will lead to improved wellbeing of communities in the Luangwa valley and subsequently improved state of biodiversity. The LLC supports Development Objective 2 and 3 of the CDCS and will contribute to the U.S. foreign policy priority of working with partner countries to help improve their business environment..

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. description.narrative: IBTCI conducted a mid-term evaluation of the Zambia Prevention, Care, and Treatment II Project (ZPCT II) on behalf of the USAID/Zambia Population, Health, and Nutrition Office. IBTCI designed an evaluation methodology that employed mixed methods, and included in-depth discussions in five outlying provinces - which include urban and rural districts - where the team interviewed staff from the National HIV/AIDS/STI/TB Council, central Ministry of Health (MOH), and the Ministry of Community Development, Maternal and Child Health, and conducted site visits to health centers and hospitals in each district that provide a number of different HIV/AIDS services. IBTCI drafted an evaluation report which provides recommendations for achieving the stated project objectives and sustainability of ZPCT II initiatives.

title.narrative: Mid-Term Evaluation of the Communications Support for Health (CSH) Program

description.narrative: IBTCI was contracted to perform a mid-term performance evaluation of USAID/Zambias Communication Support for Health (CSH) Project. CSH is tasked with supporting the GRZs vision of equity of access to assured quality, cost-effective, and affordable health services as close to the family as possible by providing technical assistance to the GRZ in strengthening national health communications activities. The aim is for GRZ health communications activities supported by CSH to translate into increased sustainable local capacity and positive behavior change that contribute to GRZ efforts in five focal areas: 1) HIV/AIDS, 2) malaria, 3) family planning/ reproductive health (FP/RH), 4) maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) and 5) nutrition. The evaluation sought to help determine what progress CSH has made in achieving its life-of-project targets and whether or not they are likely to achieve them by the end of the program. The evaluation did this by looking at what components of the CSH program were working well and to explain why this was so. If there were parts that were not working well the evaluation went further to find out why. The evaluation team used multiple methods for collecting and analyzing the data. The evaluation team used a six-phase approach, which included a document review; key informant interviews, focus group discussions, a mini survey, an online survey, and a Systems/Data Quality Assessment (DQA).

title.narrative: Mid-Term Evaluation of the Partnership for Integrated Social Marketing (PRISM) Program

description.narrative: IBTCI was contracted to conduct an evaluation of the Partnership for Integrated Social Marketing Program (PRISM), a 5-year USAID funded project which conducts social marketing programs for health services and products in HIV prevention, family planning, malaria, and maternal and child health. The evaluation employed a mix of quantitative and qualitative methods including a document review, as well as primary data collection through more than 150 key informant interviews (KIIs), 40 focus group discussions (FGDs) and 240 quantitative household surveys conducted in selected communities in two districts across six provinces. Quantitative data was analyzed using Epi-info while qualitative data was analyzed using N-Vivo. Where possible and results insightful, data was segregated by gender, age, region, urban versus rural across all PRISM products and services.

title.narrative: Prevention, Care, and Treatment Partnership II

description.narrative: In collaboration with the Government of Zambia, the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Community Development and Mother and Child Health, the Zambia Care and Treatment Partnership (ZPCT II) is being implemented in six provinces to strengthen the national health system by maximizing access, equity, quality and sustainability in the delivery of comprehensive HIV/AIDS services. The project implements strategies designed to initiate, scale up and strengthen a comprehensive package of HIV/AIDS services, including testing and counseling, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, clinical care, male circumcision and antiretroviral therapy, which are supported by strengthened laboratory and pharmaceutical systems. ZPCT IIs comprehensive approach involves integrating services; engaging communities, partners and stakeholders; building public-private partnerships; and strengthening major system components affecting the delivery of all services.

title.narrative: Support to the HIV/AIDS Response in Zambia (SHARe II)

description.narrative: Support to the HIV/AIDS Response in Zambia (SHARe II) is a continuation of the work begun in 2004, and the overall assistance objective remains to strengthen and support the mutisectoral response to HIV & AIDS in Zambia. The previous project built a solid foundation of systems, tools, communications, and information sharing and policies. This next phase of the project is focusing on the continuation of enhanced assistance, with an emphasis on quality, equitable implementation, and leadership accountability, with an added emphasis on the documenting and sharing of best practices. The project is examining and working to address the structural drivers of HIV as well as the behavioral drivers of the disease. SHARe II supports the Government of Republic of Zambia (GRZ)'s vision of "a nation free from the threat of HIV," and is working in partnership with the National HIV/AIDS/STI/TB Council, cooperating partners (including the Global Fund, UNFPA, DfID, and other bilateral, multilateral, and private sector partners), and other stakeholders to support efforts to mitigate the impact of HIV in Zambia.
